patch.value: The MCP server never receives the harness provenance environment, so one agent session writes permanently divergent identity records depending on which surface it used

Harness provenance dimensions are resolved from the process environment of whichever pm process performs the mutation. The CLI runs as a child of the harness's tool-execution path and inherits the harness's live environment. The pm MCP server is a long-lived process the harness spawns once at session start, with a different and smaller environment, and it captures process.env at that point. The two surfaces therefore see different signal sets for the same session, and because history is append-only and hash-chained, the divergence is permanent.

Verified 2026-07-31 under Claude Code with three independent observations that agree.

First, the environments differ. The pm MCP server process (node ./plugins/pm-claude/scripts/pm-mcp-server.mjs) has no CLAUDE_EFFORT in /proc/<pid>/environ. The bash tool subprocess in the same session has CLAUDE_EFFORT=xhigh. The harness exports the reasoning-level signal to tool subprocesses and not to MCP server subprocesses.

Second, the recorded provenance differs, for the same agent instance. Two items were created in one sandbox tracker within 30 seconds, one through the CLI and one through the MCP pm_create tool. Both entries carry author harness:claude-code, author_source detected, and the identical agent_instance 4cc69f82c87e6e8164c8f176, so this is one continuous session and not a session-boundary artifact. The CLI entry records agent_provenance {model: null, effort: {value: "xhigh", source: "environment"}}. The MCP entry records agent_provenance {model: null} with no effort key at all.

Third, the loss is unrecoverable rather than merely absent, which is tracked separately as pm-40scov: resolveAgentProvenance in src/core/shared/author.ts:451-455 writes an explicit null only for the model dimension, so a missing effort key cannot be distinguished from an entry written before effort support shipped.

The consequence is that every consumer of the immutable record that groups by agent_instance sees a session whose reasoning level flickers in and out of existence with no way to attribute the gaps. That directly degrades the trajectory projection in pm-qd6gvf, the episode substrate in pm-li2fj5, and any RL or evaluation workflow that needs a stable per-episode identity, because reasoning level is exactly the variable such workflows hold constant or sweep. It also breaks the read of pm-ffz0a9 in an important way: that item argues the harness does not publish the model anywhere, which remains true, but effort IS published and the MCP surface still fails to record it, so the gap is not only upstream.

Environment-snapshot-at-spawn is the deeper half. Reasoning level is mutable within a session; a user can change it mid-session. Any dimension resolved from a snapshot taken at spawn is frozen at its spawn value for the life of the server, so even if the harness did export the signal to the MCP process, entries written an hour apart would report a stale value with source environment and no indication of staleness.

A mutation written through the MCP surface records the same provenance dimensions as an identical mutation written through the CLI in the same session, proved by a paired test that compares the two history entries field by field; The MCP server resolves environment-derived provenance at mutation time rather than from a snapshot captured at spawn, so a dimension that changes mid-session is recorded with its value at the moment of the mutation; When a signal is genuinely unavailable on the MCP surface, the entry records it as explicitly unavailable rather than omitting the key, so a consumer can tell absence from unobservability; A check fails when a provenance dimension is reachable on one surface and unreachable on another, so a newly declared dimension cannot reintroduce the split; The 471 existing effort-bearing entries and the MCP-written entries in the same instances are given a stated disposition, since the record cannot be rewritten
One session produces one consistent identity record regardless of which surface wrote each entry.

The same agent_instance records effort xhigh on CLI-written entries and no effort dimension at all on MCP-written entries, permanently, because the MCP server process is spawned without CLAUDE_EFFORT and snapshots its environment at startup.

value.text: Reading /proc/<pid>/environ for a long-lived MCP server and comparing it to the tool subprocess's environment turns an inference about missing signals into a fact. Harnesses do not export the same environment to every child they spawn, so any capability that resolves configuration from process.env behaves differently per surface, and a server that snapshots env at startup freezes anything the user can change mid-session.
